items.followUp: What is the main purpose of classifying organisms?

rubric.description: States that organisms are arranged into groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the grouping of organisms.

rubric.why: Groups are based on shared and differing characteristics.
rubric.description: Mentions similarities and differences as the basis for grouping.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the basis of classification.

modelAnswer: Classification is the arrangement of organisms into groups on the basis of their similarities and differences.

items.followUp: What is taxonomy, and how does it differ from systematics?

rubric.why: Taxonomy deals with identifying, naming and classifying organisms.
rubric.description: Defines taxonomy through identification, naming or classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the role of taxonomy.

rubric.why: Systematics considers relationships among organisms as well as their diversity.
rubric.description: Distinguishes systematics by its study of organismal relationships.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the distinguishing feature of systematics.

modelAnswer: Taxonomy is the identification, naming and classification of organisms.
Systematics is the study of the diversity of organisms and their relationships.

items.followUp: State two other statements included in the cell theory.

rubric.why: Cell theory states that living organisms are made of cells.
rubric.description: States that organisms are composed of cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this cell-theory statement.

rubric.why: Cell theory states that new cells come from pre-existing cells.
rubric.description: States that cells arise from pre-existing cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this cell-theory statement.

modelAnswer: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells.
New cells arise from pre-existing cells.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of the cell membrane according to the fluid mosaic model.

rubric.why: The membrane is formed by a phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the bilayer component.

rubric.why: Proteins are embedded in the bilayer and can move within it, giving the membrane its mosaic and fluid nature.
rubric.description: States that proteins are embedded in and move within the bilayer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the protein arrangement and mobility.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane consists of a phospholipid bilayer.
Proteins are embedded in the bilayer and can move within it, making the membrane fluid and mosaic.

items.followUp: What is metastasis, and which type of tumour can undergo it?

rubric.why: Benign tumours remain localized and do not invade nearby tissues.
rubric.description: States that benign tumours remain localized.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the benign-tumour feature.

rubric.why: Malignant tumours invade tissues and can spread to other parts of the body.
rubric.description: States that malignant tumours can spread.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the malignant-tumour feature.

modelAnswer: Benign tumours remain localized and do not spread to other parts of the body.
Malignant tumours invade nearby tissues and can spread to other parts of the body.

items.followUp: How does substrate binding affect the shape of an enzyme in the induced fit model?

rubric.why: The induced fit model describes a flexible enzyme active site.
rubric.description: States that the active site is flexible.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the flexibility of the active site.

rubric.why: Binding of the substrate causes the active site to change shape to fit it.
rubric.description: States that substrate binding changes the active-site shape to fit the substrate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the induced-fit change.

modelAnswer: In the induced fit model, an enzyme's active site is flexible.
When the substrate binds, the active site changes shape to fit the substrate.

items.followUp: Name two conditions that can cause an enzyme to denature.

rubric.why: Denaturation involves a change in the enzyme's structure.
rubric.description: Identifies the structural change involved in denaturation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the change.

rubric.why: The altered active site can no longer function properly, so the enzyme becomes inactive.
rubric.description: States that the altered active site makes the enzyme inactive.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the effect on enzyme activity.

modelAnswer: Denaturation is a change in an enzyme's structure that alters its active site.
The enzyme then becomes inactive and cannot function properly.

items.followUp: How does ATP provide energy for cellular activities?

rubric.why: ATP is the cell's immediate energy source or energy currency.
rubric.description: Identifies ATP as a source or carrier of energy for the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for ATP's energy role.

rubric.why: ATP supplies energy to drive cellular activities.
rubric.description: States that ATP powers cellular activities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining what the energy is used for.

modelAnswer: ATP acts as the cell's immediate energy source and transfers energy where it is needed.
It provides energy for cellular activities.
